title: Independent predictors of time from symptom onset to discharge among patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome: a retrospective cohort study
abstract: Background Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) is a tick-borne bunyaviral infection with heterogeneous recovery trajectories and high case fatality. Most prior studies use in-hospital mortality as the primary endpoint; few quantify independent predictors of recovery duration among surviving patients. This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory factors independently associated with total time from symptom onset to hospital discharge to guide risk stratification and targeted intervention. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort analysis of 43 consecutive laboratory-confirmed SFTS survivors discharged from Taizhou Hospital of Zhejiang Province (July 2019–April 2025). Demographics, laboratory values, and organ involvement data were extracted from electronic medical records. The primary outcome was total days from initial symptom onset to meeting standardized discharge criteria. Univariate correlation and group comparisons screened candidate variables; backward stepwise multiple linear regression was applied to identify independent predictors after multicollinearity diagnosis via variance inflation factor (VIF). Model performance was assessed using adjusted coefficient of determination (adjusted R 2 ). All statistical tests were two-sided (α=0.05). Results The mean total recovery duration was 16.58 ± 7.86 days. Univariate analysis demonstrated significant correlations between longer discharge time and three variables: prolonged platelet decline duration (r=0.6577, P<0.0001), delayed hospital admission after symptom onset (r=0.7441, P<0.0001), and presence of cardiac/circulatory involvement (P = 0.0002). Multivariate regression confirmed three independent predictors: platelet decline duration (β=0.63, P = 0.0001), cardiac/circulatory involvement (β=5.33, P = 0.0003), and days from onset to hospitalization (β=1.41, P<0.001). The final model had an adjusted R 2 of 0.7762, explaining 77.62% of variance in recovery time; all included variables had VIF<2.5 without severe multicollinearity. Conclusions Prolonged platelet decline duration, cardiovascular organ injury, and delayed hospital admission after symptom onset independently prolong hospitalization duration among discharged SFTS survivors. Dynamic monitoring of platelet counts and cardiovascular biomarkers enables risk stratification. Early hospital presentation, targeted platelet support, and cardioprotective management may shorten disease courses and optimize medical resource utilization for SFTS patients.

full_text: Abstract Background Endemic–epidemic time-series models partition surveillance counts into endemic, within-area and neighbor-associated components; for directly transmitted diseases a large neighbor-associated component is often read as evidence of geographic spread. Scrub typhus, Japanese spotted fever and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome are acarine-borne zoonoses in which sustained person-to-person transmission does not occur, so they provide a biologically motivated negative-control setting for interpreting short-lag associations between human notifications as transmission between areas. Methods We analyzed weekly notifications of the three infections for the 47 prefectures of Japan, 2013–2025, fitting negative-binomial endemic–epidemic models under five area-baseline specifications, from a single national intercept to prefecture-specific effects. Simulations crossed baseline structure and coupling strength, with identical generating and fitted spatial operators in the principal reference grid; disease-calibrated simulations used row-normalized adjacency for generation and binary adjacency for fitting, matching the empirical specification. Results The neighbor-associated fraction under a single national intercept was 0.235 (approximate 95% interval 0.211–0.259) for Japanese spotted fever, 0.151 (0.132–0.172) for scrub typhus and 0.149 (0.120–0.180) for severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome; under prefecture-specific baselines these fell to below 0.001, 0.063 and 0.002. In simulation with coupling set to zero, spatially smoothed baseline heterogeneity produced mean fractions of 0.083 under the common-intercept estimator in the reference grid and 0.027–0.060 in simulations calibrated to each disease—18–40% as large as the empirical estimates—and four additional zero-coupling mechanisms yielded mean fractions of 0.069–0.112 under the common-intercept estimator. With genuine coupling (true fraction 0.142) the common-intercept estimator returned 0.224 whereas prefecture-specific baselines returned 0.141 when the fitted spatial operator matched the generating one. Conclusions The estimated neighbor-associated fraction changed substantially with the specification of background risk, shared temporal structure and spatial weights; appreciable fractions arose with no between-area coupling, and recovery of genuine coupling depended on alignment between generating and fitted spatial operators. Neighbor-associated fractions should be treated as specification-dependent summaries of statistical dependence, reported across alternative baselines and weights and corroborated with independent data before being interpreted as transmission. full_text: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) and Rickettsia monacensis, transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicornis and Ixodes spp. ticks respectively, are endemic to East Asia and can cause overlapping febrile illnesses. Despite their shared ecological niches, co-infections remain poorly characterized. This study investigated the prevalence of R. monacensis co-infection in patients with SFTS in Korea using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and sequencing. Clinical samples were collected from 129 patients with SFTS. One-step reverse-transcription PCR was performed to identify the SFTS virus (SFTSV), and rickettsial nested PCR testing targeted outer membrane protein A (ompA). Phylogenetic analysis was conducted to confirm the evolutionary relationships among the different species. Among the 129 SFTS cases, nine patients with SFTSV were positive for R. monacensis, with a prevalence rate of 7.9%. Phylogenetic tree analysis revealed that the seven sequences identified in the present study clustered closely with R. monacensis. title: Microscopically identified tick-borne hemoparasites in cattle and Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus in Hyalomma ticks in northern Côte d’Ivoire
abstract: Ticks and tick-borne diseases are major One Health threats, affecting animal and human health and imposing substantial economic burdens. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of tick-borne hemoparasites in cattle and to assess Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) in ticks in three departments of northern Côte d’Ivoire. A cross-sectional survey was conducted to collect whole blood from cattle and ticks removed from the same animals. Giemsa-stained blood smears were microscopically examined for the detection and morphological identification of hemoparasites, while tick pools were tested for CCHFV RNA by RT-qPCR. In total, 96 cattle were sampled, yielding 561 ticks (7 nymphs and 554 adults). Five tick species were identified: Amblyomma variegatum , Hyalomma rufipes , Hyalomma truncatum , Rhipicephalus annulatus , and Rhipicephalus microplus . Amblyomma variegatum was the predominant species. Five hemoparasites were microscopically identified, including Babesia bovis , Babesia bigemina , Anaplasma marginale , Anaplasma centrale , and Theileria annulata , with an overall prevalence of 34.38% (95% CI: 25.48–44.52%). Babesia bovis was the most prevalent species (18.75%, 95% CI: 12.07–27.94%), whereas Babesia bigemina was the least frequently detected (2.08%, 95% CI: 0.51–8.08%). CCHFV was detected in 2 of the 9 Hyalomma tick pools analyzed. These findings provide updated epidemiological data on tick infestation, tick-borne hemoparasite infections, and CCHFV RNA detection in Hyalomma tick pools from sampled cattle herds in northern Côte d’Ivoire. Further molecular and longitudinal studies are needed to better characterize the epidemiology of these pathogens and their potential impact on animal and public health.
